target_customer: Colombian households buying frozen ready meals; later food brands in Colombia and Mexico that pay for distribution and logistics
problem: Healthy prepared food was hard to buy affordably in Latin America, and prepared food brands lacked multichannel distribution and cold chain logistics.
business_model: Direct to consumer frozen meal subscription at the start; now a commercial and logistics partner charging 6 to 14 percent of sales to food brands

founders.name: Mateo Cardenas Huertas
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he spent several years building business models and technology for the food industry; no employers or education listed.

founders.name: Santiago Espinosa
education: M.A. and B.A. in Economics (institutions not named on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC bio lists these ventures; Forbes Colombia confirms EnLaU and Delirato were earlier companies he and his co-founder started.

competitors.name: LivUp
competitors.what: Brazilian healthy prepared meal delivery that added ready to eat food

competitors.name: Home Chef
competitors.what: US meal kit and prepared meal delivery company cited by Forbes Colombia as a comparable

competitors.name: Foody
competitors.what: Bogota healthy semi prepared meal subscription co-founded in 2017 that Todos Comemos later bought
competitors.traction_then: monthly losses over US$20,000 before integration

technical_complexity.rationale: Frozen meal production and ordering are conventional; the hard parts are cold chain logistics and food operations rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: Meal brands are easy to copy, but owning multi temperature distribution centers and retail relationships in Colombia and Mexico later built some operational scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it per sources; instead the company bought Foody in August 2021 and later pivoted to serving established brands such as Alpina and NotCo.

market_need_then: Forbes Colombia reports the company sized its market at about US$100 billion and aimed to replace part of what households eat; pandemic era demand for delivered food supported launch in 2020. Independent demand data not found.

branding.name_origin: Spanish for We All Eat; the Colombian agency El Engalle built the identity on the literal meaning.
branding.domain_note: todoscomemos.com, exact name .com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Symbol built around the idea that anyone can be a great cook at home, per the agency description
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, family and mission driven (donates 7 percent of sales to Colombia's food bank per Forbes Colombia)

branding.brand_signature: Food bank donation of 7 percent of sales

rebrands.to: Todos Comemos (new identity by El Engalle)
rebrands.why: Agency case study describes a rebrand project launched July 2020; the earlier look is not described

branding.community_and_virality: Wefunder community round with 86 investors was reported; no evidence of memes or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear Spanish name and agency designed identity, but the company later became a B2B distributor, so the consumer brand was not a major growth driver.

pivots.from: Direct to consumer frozen meal subscription
pivots.to: Distribution and logistics for third party food brands (stated on current site)
pivots.why: Company site now presents it as a commercial and operational partner; the exact date and reason for the shift are not stated by sources

outcome_analysis: Todos Comemos is still active and grew to about 62 people after YC Summer 2020. It bought Foody in August 2021 to add production capacity, then shifted toward distributing other food brands with eight distribution centers and 12,500 points of sale claimed on its site. Funding is only partly verified, so the outcome is unclear beyond stable operations.
notes: Seed amount conflict: StartupIntros says $1M announced 2021-09-01 with 11 investors (including a16z, General Catalyst, FTX Ventures and athletes); Shizune lists $1.3M dated 2021-10; Forbes Colombia says the company was still in its seed round in August 2021 and names no investors. Investor list copied from StartupIntros and partly unverified (FTX Ventures and others omitted from the round list). An earlier $240K seed dated 2020-08 appears only on StartupIntros so it is unverified and not a round. Wefunder reported $53,871 from 86 investors. CB Insights total of $180K conflicts. Foody price was over COP 2 billion (about US$500K) per Forbes Colombia; one YC news item gives a conflicting date. Competitor sources are dated August 2021, about one year after the batch; no contemporaneous 2020 competitor sources were found.
